    Before the DanceWarren's baseball aranciniHave you seen my baseball? asks Warren. Crumbed risotto balls, mozzarella middle, marinara.How to make it30g butter1 brown onion, finely diced300g arborio rice1 L hot vegetable stock50g parmesan, finely grated125g mozzarella, cut in 12 cubes75g plain flour2 eggs, beaten120g dry breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for frying400g jar passata2 garlic cloves, crushed1 small bunch basilSoften the onion in the butter, stir in the rice, then add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until creamy and just tender.Stir in the parmesan, season, spread on a tray and chill until firm.Roll into 12 balls, pushing a cube of mozzarella into the middle of each.Roll in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.Simmer the passata with the garlic and a few basil leaves while the oil heats.Fry the arancini at 180°C in batches until deep golden, drain and serve with the marinara and torn basil.Pat Healy's architect garlic knotsHealy tells Mary he's an architect. Garlic butter knots, parmesan, marinara.How to make it500g ball pizza dough60g butter4 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp parsley, chopped30g parmesan, finely grated300ml marinara sauceCut the dough into 12 strips, roll each into a rope and tie in a loose knot.Prove on a lined tray for 10 minutes, then bake at 220°C until golden.Melt the butter with the garlic for a minute and stir in the parsley.Toss the hot knots in the garlic butter and parmesan and serve with warm marinara.Prom night cheese ball and crackersFor the photos Ted never got.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.The Main EventWarren's franks and beansTed's prom night zipper disaster. Smoky franks, molasses baked beans, slaw.How to make it8 smoked frankfurts3 rashers of smoky bacon, chopped1 brown onion, diced2 x 400g tins of cannellini beans, drained400g tin crushed tomatoes3 tbsp molasses2 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp Dijon mustard1 tbsp cider vinegar250ml water200g coleslaw mix3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaiseFry the bacon and onion in an ovenproof pot until soft and golden.Stir in the beans, tomatoes, molasses, sugar, mustard, vinegar and water and bring to a simmer.Bake uncovered at 170°C, stirring once, until thick and dark.Toss the slaw with the mayo, and grill the franks until blistered.Serve the franks on the beans with slaw alongside.Puffy's body-cast chicken cordon bleuPuffy ends up in a full body cast. Ham and swiss chicken, crumbed, mustard cream.How to make it4 chicken breasts4 slices of leg ham4 slices of Swiss cheese50g plain flour2 eggs, beaten120g panko breadcrumbs3 tbsp olive oil200ml thickened cream1 tbsp wholegrain mustard150g green beansCut a deep pocket into each breast and fill with a folded slice of ham and cheese.Dust in flour, dip in egg and press into the panko.Brown in the oil on both sides, then bake at 200°C until cooked through.Warm the cream with the mustard and season, and steam the beans.Slice the chicken and serve with the beans and the mustard cream.Last Dance SweetsHair gel meringues with lemon curdMary thinks it's hair gel. Vanilla meringues, whipped cream, lemon curd.How to make it3 egg whites175g caster sugar1 tsp white vinegar1 tsp cornflour1 tsp vanilla extract300ml thickened cream200g lemon curd125g blueberriesWhisk the whites to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoon at a time until thick and glossy.Whisk in the vinegar, cornflour and vanilla and spoon 8 swirled mounds onto lined trays.Bake at 120°C until crisp outside, then turn the oven off and let them cool inside.Whip the cream with a little vanilla, and top each meringue with cream, lemon curd and blueberries.The Punch BowlSenior prom punchMary asks Ted to the prom. Pineapple, ginger beer, rum and lime sorbet.How to make it180ml white rum500ml pineapple juice500ml ginger beer2 limes, juiced4 scoops of lime sorbet1 tray iceStir the rum, pineapple and lime juice in a punch bowl with ice.Top with the ginger beer.Float the sorbet on top and ladle into cups.Beer.
